analysis: Amendment 6 (pre-registered): capability pilot for gpt-6-luna. Descriptive only, not inferential.
design: Same 41 SWE-bench Verified instances as the primary pilot, k=1, same scaffold, same 40-step limit, harness gold.

comparison_same_41_instances_uncondition.note: Our own run and the public run agree to 0.2 points, which validates the comparison. An earlier figure of 33.3% for gpt-5-mini was the unselected-arm rate, which conditions on producing a non-empty patch and so is not comparable; counting empty patches as failures, as the leaderboard does, gives 48.6%.

instrument_failure_7.symptom: 0 of 41 trajectories submitted a patch; every one exited RepeatedFormatError after 3 API calls.
instrument_failure_7.false_reading: That gpt-6-luna cannot drive an agent scaffold - the same conclusion reached for local 7B/14B agents.
instrument_failure_7.cause: Our config forced model_class: litellm, which unconditionally sends native function tools. gpt-6-luna rejects function tools on /v1/chat/completions (they conflict with its implicit reasoning effort); with drop_params: true litellm silently dropped the tools, the model replied in correct text, and the model class - which parses only tool calls - saw none and aborted. Switching to the text-based config did not help because our config overrode its model class too.
instrument_failure_7.caught_by: Sending the agent's own system+user prompt directly to the model, which returned exactly the expected format. Fixed by model_class: litellm_response (the Responses API, where the model does support tools).
instrument_failure_7.rule_reaffirmed: A rate of exactly 0% or 100% is an instrument, not a result.

consequence.caveat: A more capable agent produces fewer silent failures (committed rate ~16% vs our 35%), so ~212 instances are needed to reach the 35 failures the current study has. Cheapness solves the budget problem, not the statistical one.
